title: FindFirstChild()
summary: Non-yielding lookup: returns the child with that name, or nil if absent. The safe, crash-proof alternative to direct indexing (parent.ChildName) whenever existence isn't guaranteed.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Search the whole subtree, not just direct children.

reference.returns: The child, or nil. Siblings with the same name: returns the first found (order not guaranteed).

details.heading: Family of lookups
details.body: FindFirstChildOfClass(className) — first child of an exact class. FindFirstChildWhichIsA(className) — class or subclass. Both non-recursive direct-child scans.

explanation.whatItIs: The polite knock: 'is there a child named X?' — answer comes back instantly as an object or nil, never as a crash.
explanation.whyItExists: Direct indexing `parent.X` ERRORS when X is missing. FindFirstChild converts 'missing' into a value you can branch on.
whenToUse: Checks before use: `local h = char:FindFirstChild("Humanoid") if h then …`
Feature detection (does this model have a 'Seat'?)
Anywhere absence is possible or meaningful
whenNotToUse: Waiting for something that WILL arrive — WaitForChild
Deep searches across huge trees — GetDescendants or tags are better designs
tips: Idiom: `local x = parent:FindFirstChild("X"); if not x then return end`
For classes: FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") beats name guessing
Truthiness: `if parent:FindFirstChild("Coin") then` is a valid existence test
commonMistakes: Calling a method on the result without a nil check — FindFirstChild can ALWAYS return nil
Assuming which duplicate-named child comes back
Using recursive=true as a crutch for a disorganized hierarchy

examples.title: Touched-handler safety
examples.code:
part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    -- hit.Parent might be anything — check before touching:
    local humanoid = hit.Parent and hit.Parent:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if humanoid then
        humanoid:TakeDamage(10)
    end
end)
examples.whyItWorks: Two guards: hit.Parent could be nil-ish for terrain/effects, and only characters have Humanoids. No crash path.
